title: How an Electric Car Works in 60 Seconds 🔋⚡ #shorts
description:
A typical electric car turns about 87 to 91 percent of its battery energy into motion, compared with about 30 percent for a gasoline car. A big battery feeds an inverter, the inverter powers the motor, and when you slow down the motor charges the battery again. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#electriccar #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: Efficiency
steps.text: A typical electric car turns about *90 percent* of its battery energy into motion. A gas car manages about 30.

steps.label: Battery
steps.text: Under the floor sits a huge *battery pack*, built from hundreds or even thousands of cells.

steps.label: Inverter
steps.text: The battery gives *direct current*. An inverter flips it into alternating current for the motor.

steps.label: Motor
steps.text: In the *motor*, that current makes a spinning magnetic field that drags the rotor around.

steps.label: One Gear
steps.text: Most electric cars use just *one gear* to send that spin to the wheels.

steps.label: Regen
steps.text: Lift off the pedal and the motor becomes a *generator*, charging the battery as you slow down.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Battery, inverter, *motor*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
